reading.a: A man in a bright yellow jacket (element 3, box [103, 0, 540, 799]) peeks out from behind a tree trunk at the left (element 1, box [0, 0, 224, 799], the nearest element), against soft green and white bokeh.
reading.b: A café snapshot: the man nearest the camera stands at the left holding up a phone (element 10, box [0, 268, 432, 799]), a woman in green behind his raised hand, a woman in black smiling at the right, in front of a cream brick wall and a monstera.

concepts.idea: With no camera move, in one continuous motion: the tree slides out to the left (t 0.03-0.40, 0.1-1.2 s) while the café, its wall, monstera and both women, arrives behind the man brightest-first (t 0.03-0.50, 0.1-1.5 s); from t 0.10 (0.3 s), while the tree is still leaving, the man glides onto the nearest man's place over the café, his face onto k1's face, landing at about t 0.61 (1.8 s); he turns to the camera as himself (k1, about t 0.68, 2.0 s), takes the nearest man's pose and raised phone with his own face (k3, about t 0.78, 2.3 s) and becomes the nearest man as he is in the last frame (t 1.0, 3.0 s); B's man is not seen anywhere before ours lands on his place.

anchors.how: His pairing, unchanged: the yellow man goes to the person nearest the camera.

transforms.name: bokeh_to_cafe
transforms.note: The lead, not a beat; unchanged from round 11: A's bokeh takes the café wall's and the monstera's colours and ends with the café's arrival at t 0.5.

transforms.name: tree_goes_away
transforms.note: Beat 1, his 'the tree from frame A go away', starting at t 0.03 instead of 0.05 and ending at 0.40 instead of 0.45 so it overlaps the glide from t 0.10. Answers 'When starting to move man in frame A you reveal man in B (because of tear in frame A': hole_reveal false (the round-11 plan's value; the page's round-11 clip had the operator's hole_reveal=true) and the concept's reveal guard keep B's man out of the trunk's place: the guard holds A's base inside B's man's matte, grown by 1 % of the width, until the chain's lead lands (its default arrive). Where the trunk's place lies outside B's man, the café arrives there with the end effect.

transforms.name: man_becomes_nearest_man
transforms.note: Beats 2 and 3: the glide (the chain's rigid lead) and the identity change (k1, k3, then B). Answers 'all happen with weird pauses and in very linear way': one chain window from t 0.10 to the last frame under the trapezoid (edge 0.35), so the man speeds up out of A, keeps moving through every keyframe and slows only onto B; times 'arc' sets the knots by each segment's displacement so the glide and the steps run at one visual speed; k2 (B's man in a yellow shirt) is dropped, so there is one dissolve fewer and the face and the shirt change together in the last segment (retrospective rule 6), which answers 'transform shape, transform face and finalize rest of image' as separate steps. The clip's last beat ends at 1.0, so no still frames at the end (round 11 held 7). Answers the tear with the guard (arrive = the lead's landing). Spans, computed from round 11's measured segment displacements (lead 283 px, lead to k1 31 px, k1 to k3 72.2 px; k3 to B assumed below the floor of 0.2 of the largest) and the trapezoid: chain knots 0.60, 0.73, 0.88; in clip time the lead lands at about t 0.61 (1.8 s), k1 at about 0.68, k3 at about 0.78, B at 1.0. What remains by construction: the glide is still a rigid move of A's man (rule 3, T45) and the segments between faces are face-aligned dissolves (rules 6 and 7, T40).

helper.what: Two generated in-betweens of the man only, used inside his matte: A's man turned to the camera at B's man's place (k1) and A's face on B's man's body with the phone in a yellow T-shirt (k3); k2 of round 11 is not used. The café, the two women, the tree and the bokeh come from the two photos, and both end frames are original.

knobs.name: man_becomes_nearest_man.params.arc_floor
knobs.what: The share of the largest segment's displacement that a segment without motion still gets in the arc times; higher shortens the rigid glide and gives the two face dissolves more time (0.2 gives the glide about 0.60 of the chain, 0.5 about 0.40).

knobs.name: end_effect.window
knobs.what: When the café arrives behind the man; it should be complete beside him while he glides, or A's plate shows beside him.

knobs.name: guard
knobs.what: The reveal guard; false shows the round-11 behaviour, B's man visible where the tree leaves before our man lands (his tear frame).

concepts.risk: Rule 3 (a moving subject deforms): with arc times the rigid glide takes about 0.60 of the chain, about 1.5 s against round 11's 0.41 s, so the cut-out move he named ('you cut out yellow man , move him onto man B') is longer and easier to see; look at t 0.1-0.6 and try arc_floor 0.5. Rule 1 (no B before its beat): the guard covers B's man only (element 10 grown by 1 %); his raised phone hand or the woman in green behind it can still show through the trunk's place before t 0.5 if they lie outside that matte; read b_inside_first and the guard share in info.json. Rule 5 (no edge in neither photo): until the lead lands, A's plate (an inpainted fill) shows inside B's man's matte where neither man covers it; its outline is B's man's silhouette and may read as a pale shape at t 0.3-0.6; read residual_edge_max. Rules 6 and 7: k1 to k3 and k3 to B are face-aligned dissolves (round 11 showed a phone without a hand and a torn hand ghost in k1 to k3, rule 8). Rule 7: the café's arrival is still a brightest-first dissolve of the bokeh. F3 invention: k1 and k3 are generated; the page must say so.
